lede: Validation MSE falls until latent 16–32. Latent 128 is the lowest point and the scored checkpoint.
title: Autoencoder compression
question: How does latent size change reconstruction error on MNIST digits?
process: Autoencoder.forward is a deterministic code. encode compresses the 784 pixels, decode maps the code back, and the two are composed:
The training step is mean squared error, the line loss = mse(self(batch_x), batch_y):
There is no latent distribution and no KL. The compression ratio is 784 divided by the length of the code.
The saved validation curve falls from about 0.187 at latent 2 to 0.096 at latent 128. The scored checkpoint is latent 128: test MSE 0.0414, MAE 0.0771. mnist_ae.db has no completed trial.

opening.summary: Latent 128 is bold: lowest validation MSE on the saved curve, and the checkpoint that was scored. The Optuna database itself never finished.
opening.hover: Hover a latent size. The bold point is latent 128.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Latent 2 is a 392× compression. Validation MSE is 0.1867. A code that short keeps a blurry class average: the digit class may survive, the stroke does not.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Latent 4 is 196× and validation MSE is 0.1496. The bottleneck is still too small for thickness and slant, so the error stays high.

marks.answers: How could the results be improved?
marks.summary: Latent 8 is 98× and validation MSE is 0.1154. This is the steep part of the curve. The next doublings are where digits usually become recognizable.
Latent 16 is 49× and validation MSE is 0.1042. This is the start of the useful range: a code of this length can store thickness and slant.
Latent 32 is 24.5× and validation MSE is 0.0999. Recognizable digits show up around 16–32. Past this point the curve is almost flat.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Latent 64 is 12.25× and validation MSE is 0.0975. The drop from 32 is 0.0024. Extra coordinates are copying detail the decoder already approximated.

Latent 128 is bold because it is the minimum of this validation curve, MSE 0.0964, and the checkpoint that was evaluated. Compression is 6.12×. Test MSE is 0.0414 and test MAE is 0.0771. The drop from latent 32 (0.0999) to here is 0.0035, so the practical code is already in the 16–32 range. The reconstruction grid is this checkpoint: 7, 2, 1, 0, 4, and 9 stay readable and slightly soft.

reflection.worked: Measured: the training loss falls, and the latent-128 checkpoint copies the test digit at MSE 0.0414.
reflection.unexpected: Measured: validation MSE only moves from 0.0975 at latent 64 to 0.0964 at 128. The Optuna database has no finished trial, so hidden size, dropout, and learning rate have no score.
reflection.why: Measured: almost all of the drop on the saved curve is over by latent 16. Guess: a digit stroke fits in that many coordinates, so further ones have little left to store. The curve and the 0.0414 test score come from different stages.
reflection.improve: For compression, stop near latent 16–32. Finish the study before treating any other hyperparameter as tested. A sharper copy needs a different loss, not a longer code.
